The story of Anthony Stokes was supposed to have a happy ending. Instead, it ended on Tuesday with the teen's death. Police say Stokes, who had received a heart transplant, carjacked someone, broke into a home, shot at an elderly woman, led police on a high-speed chase, and then crashed his car into a pole.

In 2013, when Stokes was a teenager, his family told the media that an Atlanta hospital had rejected him for heart transplant surgery. At that time, the hospital described him in a letter as having a "history of non-compliance." Mark Bell was acting as the family's spokesman.

It was very early in the morning at Garissa University College. Most students were still sleeping. A few had woken up to go to Christian prayers. Then, the attack started. It began with an explosion and gunshots at the school's front gates around 5:30 a.m. on Thursday. The attackers continued to shoot as they moved through the campus. The Red Cross said they stopped at a girls' dormitory. At one point, the attackers burst into a room where Christians were gathered and took them hostage, according to lecturer Joel Ayora.

A white casket was at the front of New Shiloh Baptist Church in West Baltimore. A gospel choir sang for a large crowd gathered to honor Freddie Gray. The 25-year-old died in police custody 15 days after he was arrested on a weapons charge. His death from a severe spinal cord injury sparked widespread outrage toward the Baltimore Police Department. Gray's death in custody is the latest in a string of high-profile deaths involving African-Americans and law enforcement. Many have demanded answers about what happened to Gray, and his funeral drew civil rights leaders, politicians, and relatives of others who died in police custody.

I have been a chef since I was 14 years old. In 2007, a young girl my wife mentored was found eating from a trash can. This inspired me to start Food Policy Action and become active in food issues like hunger and factory farms.

One major force in this work has been "The Meatrix." This is a 2003 cartoon that makes fun of "The Matrix." It was made by the GRACE Communications Foundation and showed the public health risks and environmental harms of factory farming.

Dan Swangard is a doctor who has seen many people die in hospitals. He has watched patients hooked up to morphine and suffering from anxiety pass away over weeks or months while their scared families watched helplessly.

In 2013, Swangard was diagnosed with a rare type of metastatic cancer. To treat it, surgeons removed parts of his pancreas and liver, as well as his spleen and gallbladder. The surgery was successful, but at 48 years old, Swangard knows there is a strong chance the cancer will come back.

Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters fight the Houthis in Aden. The special forces were on the ground in noncombat roles, coordinating and guiding the battle. They also helped drop in weapons and communications equipment. Following heavy Saudi airstrikes, Houthi rebels withdrew from the presidential palace and other key parts of Aden. This withdrawal marked a reversal from the previous day, when Houthi forces had seized the palace.

A Detroit mother was arrested last month after police found two bodies in a freezer. She was charged this week with murder and torture.

Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy charged Mitchelle Angela Blair with killing her 13-year-old daughter, Stoni Ann Blair, and her 9-year-old son, Stephen Gage Berry.

According to Detroit Police Chief James Craig, a bailiff found the bodies wrapped in plastic during a court-ordered eviction on March 24. The medical examiner says Stoni died from blunt force injuries, and Stephen died from blunt force and thermal (heat) injuries.

Miami (CNN) - World heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko has an important fight coming up on April 25 against Bryant Jennings in New York. However, he is very worried about what is happening in his home country, Ukraine. He spoke to CNN from his training base in Miami. Klitschko said the crisis in Ukraine has shocked and upset him. He explained that his country is suffering because of a war with Russia, and that Ukraine has not started any aggression.

Michael Keaton hosted "Saturday Night Live" for the third time this weekend. He made small jokes about his famous roles as Beetlejuice and Batman. Keaton noted that a lot has changed since he first hosted the show in 1982, mentioning he now has a 31-year-old son and a 28-year-old girlfriend.

Fans hoping for a full revival of his characters were disappointed. The cast asked him to dress up as Batman and Beetlejuice, but he only gave short, funny one-liners in response.

Just over a month ago, a jury found Kamron Taylor guilty of murder. Early Wednesday morning, Taylor escaped from an Illinois jail. He hid outside his cell and then attacked a correctional officer who was walking by. Taylor beat the guard, took his uniform and keys, and walked out of the jail. He then drove away in the officer's brown 2012 Chevrolet Equinox SUV. Taylor, 23, was supposed to be sentenced in May. Police are still looking for him. The SUV was found around 8:30 a.m.

A New York City detective has been suspended after police say he stole $3,000 during a raid at a store in Brooklyn.

According to police, the detective, Ian Cyrus, was caught on surveillance video putting cash into a bag at the Yemen Deli and Grocery store last Friday. The detectives had gone to the store to arrest two employees for selling loose cigarettes.

The store manager, Ali Abdullah, noticed money was missing from a box. He checked the security cameras and saw the detective taking the money.

London (CNN) The Hatton Garden heist was a nightmare for safe deposit box owners and a dream for movie directors. Thieves broke into a 60-year-old safe deposit company in central London over a holiday weekend. They used heavy cutting equipment and rappelling gear. Police believe they had up to four days to steal from the boxes. The thieves got away with hundreds of thousands of pounds in gems and cash. One former police official estimates the total value at up to 200 million pounds ($300 million).

As South Africa prepares to remember the first post-apartheid elections on April 27, 1994, deadly attacks against African migrants are happening again. People are very angry about this violence on social media, using the hashtag #WeAreAfrica to demand unity. These attacks show that the country's dream of a multi-ethnic society where everyone lives with dignity seems to have failed.

In 1989, Ayatollah Khomeini called accepting a ceasefire "drinking poison" to end the eight-year war with Iraq. The war had defined his new government, the Islamic Republic, which he started just before Saddam Hussein invaded Iran. Khomeini convinced both his supporters and opponents to keep fighting. Even though Saddam wanted to stop the war, Khomeini kept it going for eight years. This helped build the Islamic Republic, but by the time the war ended, the economy was ruined and his supporters had disappeared.

The idea of sustainable development is that raw capitalism is too powerful. Global capitalism is a huge force, with the world economy doubling in size every generation. Yet, with a billion new people added every 15 years on a finite Earth, this force is now attacking the physical bases of life and the social systems that make life decent. Sustainable development offers a path out of this crisis. The reality is that raw capitalism is the economics of greed.

The United States has benefited greatly from being a space-faring nation. U.S. access to space has helped national security, the military, and the economy. The military relies on satellites for intelligence, GPS, and communications to fight terrorism and handle global threats. However, the U.S. has a problem: it relies too much on Russian technology to meet its national security needs.

On the one-year anniversary of the abduction of nearly 300 schoolgirls by Boko Haram in Nigeria, Malala Yousafzai wrote an open letter to the girls. Malala, who is 17, survived an attack by the Taliban in Pakistan because she wrote about the importance of girls going to school. In her letter, she asks the Nigerian government and the world to do more to find the girls. Nigeria recently had an election.

CNN reports that South African soldiers were sent to the Johannesburg suburb of Jeppestown on Tuesday evening. This happened as part of a new government plan to stop deadly violence against foreigners. The violence started on Friday in that area. The military helped police secure the perimeter of a local hostel. Defense Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula said the troops were needed because police were spread too thin trying to stop the attacks. She added that using the military was not a criticism of the police.

Eight Iranian border guards were killed in a fight with militants near the Pakistan border. Three of the militants were also killed. The fight happened on Monday in the town of Negur in southeastern Iran. The militants came from Pakistan. Iranian officials have asked Pakistan to catch the surviving attackers.

TripAdvisor named Providenciales in the Turks and Caicos the world's best island. The island moved up from second place last year to take the top spot. Ambergris Caye in Belize, which had been number one for two years in a row, fell out of the top ten completely this year. A TripAdvisor spokeswoman said it is hard to say why winners change, as it depends on traveler feedback.

CNN reported that details about the 2016 movie "Star Wars: Rogue One" were shared at a fan festival in Anaheim, California. Director Gareth Edwards showed a preview of the film and explained that it is an anthology movie, a term Disney uses instead of "spinoff." The movie stars Felicity Jones as a rebel soldier. The story takes place between the third and fourth "Star Wars" movies. In the film, a group of rebels goes on a dangerous mission to steal the plans for the Death Star.

Tehran, Iran (CNN) There is a Persian saying: "A good year depends on its spring." For many Iranians, the decision by Tehran and six world powers to keep talking about nuclear issues is a sign that the Persian New Year, which started on March 21, will be very good. Although some hardliners may complain, most people see this as good progress.

Ferguson, Missouri (CNN) -- Two African-American candidates, Ella Jones and Wesley Bell, won seats on the Ferguson City Council on Tuesday. This means three of the six council members are now black. The election took place on a day with heavy rain and warnings of flash floods. Voters went to the polls for the first time since August of last year, when a white police officer shot and killed unarmed black teenager Michael Brown. Before this election, very few people usually voted in these local races.

An Israeli man was killed and a woman was hurt when a 37-year-old Arab driver from East Jerusalem hit them at a bus stop near Hebrew University in Jerusalem on Wednesday night. Police say the driver intentionally struck the two people standing at a bus stop in the French Hill area. One victim, 26-year-old Shalom Yohai Cherki, died at the hospital. The other victim, a 20-year-old woman, is in serious condition. The driver has been arrested and is being investigated by the General Security Services.

A collection of art owned by the late actress Lauren Bacall is now for sale. The collection includes works by famous 20th-century artists. It was shown in Hong Kong, Paris, London, and Los Angeles before being sold in New York on March 31. Bacall died in 2014 at age 89. She became famous in 1944 with the film "To Have And Have Not," where she met her husband, Humphrey Bogart. George Clooney honored her at the 2015 Golden Globes.

Kiev, Ukraine (CNN) People are asking who is killing friends of Ukraine's former President Viktor Yanukovych. This is not a new question, but it became very important this week after two famous people were shot dead in the capital city. One was Oleg Kalashnikov, a former member of parliament who supported Yanukovych. He was killed near his apartment building on Wednesday evening.

Chile will soon recognize civil unions for same-sex couples. President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law on Monday that allows these unions. The president said this is a step toward treating homosexual and heterosexual couples equally. The law will officially start in six months. It gives legal rights to couples who live together, whether they are two men, two women, or a man and a woman. The government estimates about 2 million people will benefit from this change.

The next time you fly to Florida to visit Grandma, look out the window. Whether you are going to see the talking mouse at Disney or heading to South Beach for sun and fun, look down before you land. The Everglades look like a squishy wasteland full of things that can hurt you, like snakes, scorpions, rats, roaches, alligators, and mosquitoes. A researcher once caught 365,000 mosquitoes in a single trap in just one night.

CNN reports that ISIS fighters took over Yarmouk, a Palestinian refugee camp near Damascus. The group had been under siege and bombed by Syrian forces for over two years. In early April, ISIS militants seized the area after defeating other local militia groups. A resident told CNN that ISIS killed three people in the street. The resident said the Islamic State now controls almost all of the camp.

China has long used a "Great Firewall" to block its citizens from reading Western news or other content it dislikes. However, a new study says this is not enough. China has developed a new tool called the "Great Cannon." This tool attacks servers outside of China, including in the United States. The study's authors say China is attacking visibly and easily within other countries' borders. They believe Beijing may have expected this to cause anger internationally.

A German official says the investigation into the Germanwings Flight 9525 crash has not found a clear reason why the co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, crashed the plane. However, the official says Lubitz had suicidal thoughts before he became a pilot. Investigators have not found any notes or recordings where Lubitz explained his actions. Medical records show he was suicidal and received therapy before he ever got his pilot's license.

The leader of Yemen's Houthi rebels said on Sunday that his group would not give up. He made this promise during a televised speech, stating that his fighters would not leave the main cities or government buildings. He added that anyone expecting the group to surrender was mistaken.

This statement came more than three weeks after a Saudi-led coalition began bombing campaigns. The airstrikes are meant to push the Houthis back. The group had previously moved into the capital, Sanaa, in January and removed President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi from power.

On April 19, 1995, Timothy McVeigh drove a truck bomb into the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. The explosion killed 168 people and injured hundreds more. It remains the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in U.S. history.

The attack shocked the nation. While the scale of the tragedy was huge, the real shock was that American citizens had turned their violence against their own government in a way that had never been seen before.

If you care about something, you might protest or make a sign. How long would you keep going if no one listened? When over 200 Nigerian girls were kidnapped a year ago, millions of people joined the #BringBackOurGirls campaign on Twitter. Charles Alasholuyi was one of them, joining celebrities and world leaders. But as weeks turned into months, the girls were still missing, and the world stopped paying attention.

Barney Frank is very experienced in politics. At a recent event in Chicago, the retired congressman entertained a full house as he talked about his 45 years in public service. Frank made history by becoming the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same sex while in office. He also had strong words for politicians who hide their sexuality while voting against gay rights. When an audience member asked about a California ballot proposal that would legalize killing gay people, Frank said he did not know about the measure but told the young man not to worry about "crazy people."

A deadly attack at Garissa University College in Kenya left nearly 150 people dead and many others wounded. Gunmen attacked the campus early Thursday while students were praying, shooting randomly and taking hostages before security forces killed them. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi said the Al-Shabaab militant group claimed responsibility. This attack comes just months after Al-Shabaab killed non-Muslim workers at a Kenyan quarry. The group has been behind many attacks in the region and has recruited some Americans, especially from the Somali-American community in Minnesota.

Students at the University of Cape Town in South Africa have successfully removed a statue of British colonialist Cecil Rhodes. The students started a campaign on social media called #RhodesMustFall to demand the statue come down because they believe he represents racism. After four weeks of protests, the university received permission from the heritage authority to take the statue down. The university stated they are removing the statue to keep it safe while they decide what to do with it in the future.

Syria is a very dangerous place. An opposition group says the number of people who have died has doubled in one year. Since the civil war started, 310,000 people have been killed, according to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights. A year earlier, the number was 162,402. The United Nations says the number was 70,000 the year before that. Over half of all Syrians are very poor and need help to survive. The United Nations says food rations have been cut because not enough people are donating money.

CNN reports that Ailina Tsarnaeva was quiet as she entered a New York courtroom, but prosecutors say she was not shy about threatening a rival. According to court documents, she called a woman this summer and told her to "Leave my man alone." She also warned, "Stop looking for him. ... I know people that can put a bomb where you live." Because of who she is, prosecutors did not treat this as a joke and charged her with aggravated harassment. Tsarnaeva denies the charges. She is the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev.

A police official in Gaza said on Thursday that a door with a drawing by the famous artist Banksy was taken by police. The owner, Rabea Darduna, went to court because he sold the door for only $175, not realizing how valuable it was. The door will stay with the police in southern Gaza until a court date is set. Darduna said that when his home was destroyed last summer, he was left with almost nothing, only a doorway and a door.

A Saudi-led group is attacking Houthi rebels in Yemen. The group says it now has more control. People are running away from the fighting, and many have been hurt, including many civilians. Five days after the first attacks, the group destroyed the rebels' air defenses and the defenses of former President Ali Abdullah Saleh. They have also made almost all air bases unusable. Saudi ships now control all Yemeni ports. Only medical supplies that are not for the military are allowed to enter.

Holland manager Guus Hiddink was very angry with his own fans. During the 2-0 victory against Spain on Tuesday night, the fans booed and jeered at Andres Iniesta, who came into the game as a substitute. Hiddink called the fans' behavior a "disgrace." Spain coach Vicente del Bosque had played an experimental team, and Iniesta scored the goals that gave Spain a 2-0 win. Centre back Stefan de Vrij and midfielder Davy Klaassen scored for Holland in the first half.

Scotland will find out on May 21 if Georgia's game in September will be played without fans. UEFA, the governing body of European football, opened disciplinary proceedings against the Georgian Football Federation after fans invaded the field twice during Sunday's 2-0 loss to Germany in Tbilisi. UEFA is also investigating charges that home fans set off fireworks. Other safety issues being looked at include blocked stairs, locked gates, and a lack of body searches by staff at the Boris Paichadze Stadium.

Football agents were unsure what to do on Wednesday while waiting for news about new rules. Starting April 1, anyone can become a football agent by paying £500 for a one-year registration. The FA will then charge £250 every year after that to renew the license. Agents who already had a license were exempt from these new rules. The FA planned to put a link on their website for agents to register, but by 1pm that link was not yet available. Mel Stein believes the new rules will cause chaos. The new guidelines started after FIFA decided to stop governing agents.

Maksims Uvarenko, the Latvian goalkeeper for CSKA Sofia, has not been paid for three months. He had to ask his parents to send him money to pay his rent. Even though the club is in financial trouble, Uvarenko is impressed by the fans and their passionate support. He says the lack of money is his biggest problem at the club, and that he still has not received his salary since joining in January.

Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo are famous rivals in modern football. However, a former Brazil striker who owns a second-division US team, Fort Lauderdale Strikers, wants to change that. He wants to make his team a major global force. He has said he would use his own money to sign Lionel Messi to his team. He also wants to sign Cristiano Ronaldo.

Northampton will wait for a doctor's advice before deciding when George North can play again. The Wales wing will miss this Saturday's game against Clermont Auvergne because of a head injury. North has been knocked unconscious three times recently, including last Friday against Wasps. He is currently being checked by a brain specialist. 'We won't play him at the weekend,' said Saints director of rugby Jim Mallinder.

Cesar Azpilicueta is waiting for Chelsea to win the Barclays Premier League title. He believes they are strong because they have been at the top of the table since the very beginning of the season.

Chelsea are currently in first place, six points ahead of Manchester City. They have a game left to play. The team has been considered a favorite to win the title since August, when they won seven of their first eight games.

Mohamed Diame will play for Hull City when they visit Swansea on Saturday. The team's manager, Steve Bruce, said the Senegalese midfielder is fit to play after being out for four months with a knee injury. Diame joined Hull from West Ham in the summer for £3.5 million. His return is a big help for Hull as they fight to avoid being relegated.

Toby Alderweireld is on loan at Southampton from Atletico Madrid. His loan ends this season. Atletico Madrid's director, Jose Luis Perez Caminero, said Alderweireld will return to Atletico. The 26-year-old defender has played well for Southampton. He has said he might want to stay in the Premier League. Tottenham also likes him. But Atletico says they want him back. They also want Oliver Torres to return.

Swansea player Tom Carroll, who is on loan from Tottenham, could be out of action for up to six weeks because of ankle ligament damage. He got hurt during England Under 21s' 1-0 win over the Czech Republic last Friday. Carroll scored the only goal of the game in Prague. He has played 18 games for Swansea this season.

Franck Ribery says he cannot play against Borussia Dortmund this week because he is still injured. He admits he "can't even run." The Bayern Munich winger got hurt at the start of last month during a game against Shakhtar Donetsk, where his teammate Arjen Robben also got injured. However, Ribery hopes to return for the German Cup quarter-finals against Bayer Leverkusen later this week.

Bayern Munich captain Philipp Lahm is fit to play against Borussia Dortmund on Saturday after recovering from an ankle injury. However, the team will be without several key players. Midfielders Franck Ribery, Arjen Robben, and Javi Martinez, along with defender David Alaba, are all injured. Coach Pep Guardiola is also unsure if defender Holger Badstuber can play, and midfielder Thiago Alcantara may only be fit for a short time.

Veteran Burnley defender Michael Duff believes manager Sean Dyche could one day coach England. Dyche, 43, has built a strong reputation by turning the team's fortunes around since he arrived at Turf Moor in October 2012. He led the Clarets from the Championship to the Premier League last season. Duff believes his manager is ready to face Tottenham on Sunday.

Mauricio Pochettino has allowed Harry Kane to play in the European Under 21 Championships this summer. Roy Hodgson has confirmed that the Tottenham striker will be in Gareth Southgate's squad for the tournament in the Czech Republic, even though Kane made his senior England debut last week. Kane is also scheduled to travel to Australia and Malaysia this summer. Harry Kane, who played against Italy, will compete in the Under 21 Championships this year. Kane made his first start for England against Italy after coming off the bench and scoring against Lithuania.

Alvaro Morata, 22, joined Juventus last summer for £15.8million after struggling to get into the Real Madrid first-team. He signed a five-year contract and is happy at the Italian club. His agent, Beppe Bozzo, says Morata has no desire to return to Real Madrid. Morata has scored seven goals in 22 Serie A matches this season.

Hundreds of thousands of football fans are having trouble traveling this weekend because of an Easter rail shutdown. Over 30 Premier League and Championship games are scheduled for the long weekend, but large parts of the rail network will be closed for repairs. More than half of these games will have delays and disruptions, forcing fans to use their cars instead. The big match between Arsenal and Liverpool in London will be badly affected by the rail problems. The Labour party has accused the government of not learning from the problems on Boxing Day, when nearly a million football fans had difficult journeys to get to the stadiums.

Brentford manager Mark Warburton was happy after his team won 4-1 against Fulham in a tough west London derby at Craven Cottage. Stuart Dallas scored two goals, Alan Judge scored a great free-kick, and Jota scored a late fourth goal. This win moved Brentford to fifth place in the table with 69 points and six games left to play, keeping them in contention for the play-offs.

The Barclays Premier League has announced the final set of televised matches for the 2014-15 season. As the season reaches its end, Sky Sports and BT Sport have revealed their schedules, with the race for the Champions League featuring heavily.

The standout games include Chelsea vs Liverpool on May 10 and Manchester United vs Arsenal on May 17. Manchester United previously beat Arsenal at the Emirates earlier this season. Juan Mata scored for Manchester United in a live TV match against Liverpool last month. The TV schedule for the final day of the season, Sunday, May 24, will be announced later.

A U.S. fighter jet is flying high in the sky. It is about 70 years old. A father and son rebuilt it from more than 200 parts. They did it to honor American soldiers who died in battle. The plane is a P-51D Mustang.

Brazil's World Cup stadium in Natal is up for sale. The company that owns it, Grupo OAS, is having money problems after a corruption scandal. The company is selling the stadium, called Dunas Arena, and half of another arena in Salvador. The problems started after a corruption investigation at Petrobras, a state oil company, made it hard for the builder to get loans.

A group of U.S. senators has asked FIFA to remove Russia as the host of the 2018 World Cup. The senators, who are from both the Democratic and Republican parties, sent a letter on Tuesday. They want Russia removed because of its role in the Ukraine crisis and its occupation of Crimea.

A helicopter crashed into a house in a neighborhood near Sao Paulo, Brazil, yesterday around 5:20 pm. The crash killed five people, including Thomaz Alckmin, the son of the state governor Geraldo Alckmin.

Jos Hooiveld scored in the 87th minute to give Millwall a 2-1 win over Charlton on Good Friday. It was Millwall's first victory at Charlton's stadium since October.

Charlton's captain, Chris Solly, was sent off just before halftime for handling the ball in the box. Although Lee Gregory missed the resulting penalty, Millwall's Magaye Gueye scored later to tie the game. Hooiveld's late goal secured the win for Millwall.

It may not be as fast as a Ferrari or as fancy as a Rolls Royce, but the most popular car in the world is 50 years old this year. The simple hatchback was first designed in 1965 to help French farmers move their sheep to market. Today, it makes up two out of every three cars sold in the UK and remains popular worldwide, from Munich to Mexico City, because it is practical, economical, and comfortable. The first ever hatchback was the Renault 16, which was unveiled in April 1965. Its predecessor, the Renault 4, was also created to help French farmers transport sheep.

Venezuela captain Juan Arango apologized to a rival player after biting him on the shoulder at the end of a Mexican league match.

Arango's team, Tijuana, was losing 4-3 to Monterrey with only seconds left. He went up to midfielder Jesus Zavala and bit him.

The 34-year-old midfielder said, "I did something I shouldn't have done with Zavala."

During the game, Zavala held his shoulder and showed the referee the bite mark. Zavala's side won the match 4-3.

Paul Merson started an argument with Andros Townsend again after Townsend came onto the field with only seven minutes left in Tottenham's 0-0 draw with Burnley on Sunday. Merson tweeted, "Just been watching the game, did you miss the coach? #RubberDub #7minutes." He had previously annoyed Townsend by writing in a column that if Townsend could get into the England team, "it opens it up to anybody." Merson criticized Townsend again after his short appearance for Tottenham against Burnley.

Reports that Cristiano Ronaldo is doing badly have been wrong. The Real Madrid forward scored five goals against Granada, bringing his total for the La Liga season to 36. This is more than half of the goals scored by Europe's top teams.

Granada were beaten badly by Ronaldo and his teammates. The European champions won 9-1 at the Bernabeu, and Ronaldo scored five goals in the match. This was the first time in his career he had scored five goals in one game.

His total of 36 league goals for the season was higher than Lionel Messi's 32. It also put him in an incredible position: he had scored more goals than 53 of the 98 teams in Europe's top five leagues this season.

Hull lost to Hull KR on Thursday, but they won 28-20 against St Helens on Sunday. A long try by Jamie Shaul helped Hull win. This was surprising because St Helens were tired after playing on Good Friday. St Helens were missing some players and started two very young players. Hull took advantage of this to win the match.

Almeria, a team struggling in La Liga, has hired Sergi Barjuan as their third coach of the season. The 43-year-old replaces Juan Ignacio Martinez, who was fired on Sunday after the team lost 4-1 at home to Levante.

Almeria confirmed that if the paperwork is finished, Barjuan will coach the team's away match at Barcelona on Wednesday. Barjuan, a former Barcelona defender, made 53 international appearances for Spain between 1998 and 2004. He spent nine years at Barcelona and played in two World Cups for Spain. He previously coached Recreativo in Spain's second division from 2012 to 2014.

As Easter Sunday approaches, Christians around the world marked Good Friday, which remembers the death of Jesus Christ. "Way of the Cross" walks happened in places like Ohio, Pennsylvania, and over the Brooklyn Bridge. In Rome, tens of thousands of people joined Pope Francis' torchlight procession at the Colosseum. The Pope used the service to speak about the persecution of Christians.

On Tuesday afternoon, England fans gathered at a pub in Turin. Some went outside and sang a song that criticized the IRA. Inside the Juventus Stadium, about 2,000 England fans also sang the same song during a friendly match against Italy. There is no suggestion that the people in the picture were involved in the chanting.

A man named John, who works as a builder, posted an advertisement in the window of his local newsagent in Muswell Hill. He was looking for someone special to share "a way of life with quality." The ad, written in black capital letters, became popular online after a passerby photographed it.

Helsinborg manager Henrik Larsson had to play his 42-year-old kit man, Daniel Andersson, in goal on Saturday because the regular goalkeepers were injured. Astonishingly, Andersson kept a clean sheet as his team drew 0-0 against Kalmar. Speaking after the game, the retired goalkeeper, who earned one cap for Sweden in 2001, said he was surprised to be playing again.

Ben Jones-Bishop scored a great solo try. This helped the Salford Red Devils end a streak of 17 straight losses against Wigan. The final score was 24-18. Both teams finished the game with 12 players on the field because of fighting. Jones-Bishop, who recently joined Salford from Leeds Rhinos, scored his seventh try of the season. He scored just before halftime to help Salford move up to third place in the league table.

It has been a little over a year since Alan Pardew had an ugly argument on the sidelines with Manuel Pellegrini while he was managing Newcastle. The FA warned Pardew about his behavior, and he wrote to Pellegrini to apologize for the name he called him. On Monday at Selhurst Park, Pardew, who now manages Crystal Palace, will face Pellegrini and Manchester City again. He is trying to change a pattern of behavior he feared was becoming destructive. After getting advice from the League Managers’ Association, the 53-year-old began working with sports psychologist Jeremy Snape.

Joe Hart is staying positive about Manchester City's chances, even though some people think the title race is already decided. He points out that the team has won the league before by making a strong finish at the end, like they did in 2012 and 2014. Hart says, "It’s kind of how we do it." He admits the team hasn't played perfectly every week, but believes they still have a chance. He notes that they have eight important games left, starting with a match against Crystal Palace on Monday, to get back to the level they need to be at.

Mils Muliaina, a former rugby player who won the World Cup with New Zealand, was arrested last night. He was arrested after his team lost a match in England. The police arrested him because they suspect he sexually assaulted a woman in Cardiff in March. Muliaina denies the allegations and has since been released on bail. He is 34 years old and has played 100 games for the All Blacks.

QPR is feeling confident before their important game at Aston Villa on Tuesday. The team had lost 13 of their last 14 away games, but they broke their five-game losing streak with a 4-1 win at West Brom on Saturday. This victory moved them out of the bottom three, though they are still only three points away from safety. Coach Chris Ramsey told reporters that the team's morale is good and that they played professionally. Forward Eduardo Vargas scored the first goal in that win.

Lydia Ko played poorly on Saturday, shooting a 2-over 74. This was her second round in a row over par, following a 73 on Friday where she hit her ball into the water on the last hole.

Despite the bad score, the 17-year-old New Zealander kept two important streaks alive. She made an 8-foot birdie putt on a par-5 hole to maintain her record of making at least one birdie in every round she has played in her career. She also kept alive her streak of 29 consecutive rounds under par, which ties a record on the LPGA Tour.

Arsene Wenger has not yet decided if he will give Abou Diaby a new contract. However, he has suggested that the injury-prone midfielder might have a future at Arsenal after this summer.

Diaby recently returned from injury in a practice game on Wednesday. However, he has only played 22 times in the last five seasons because of long periods on the sidelines.

Arsenal plays Liverpool on Saturday at lunchtime. Wenger is unlikely to start Diaby in this important game. However, he said Diaby might earn a new contract, possibly one where he only gets paid when he plays.

It is very popular at the Shell Houston Open. There are record numbers of people there, even though the famous players Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy are not playing. The tournament, which happens just before the Masters, is a big hit because of Phil Mickelson and Jordan Spieth.

Spieth, who is 21, caused a stir 18 months ago when he left university to turn professional. He was ranked 809th in the world at the time. Since then, he has improved a lot and is now ranked fourth. People no longer criticize him for leaving school.
